pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour of the school office in this workspace. Share it with the principal, the office manager, the facilities lead and teachers who plan events.
: each class with its teacher, room, size, limit, seats left, absences and students joining.
: new students, transfers and withdrawals, with records, immunizations, home language and the class they join.
: each class's morning count of present, excused, unexcused and tardy.
: staff absences and who is covering.
: licenses, clearances and required training with expiry dates.
: trips, family nights, assemblies and testing windows.
Every morning: cover, the attendance call, urgent requests.
Monday: events for the next two weeks and notices to send.
Wednesday: enrollment paperwork chased; new students placed.
Friday: the principal reviews the Dashboard: chronic absence, licenses expiring, open requests.
Every morning: absences needing cover, the attendance count, calls home
Every week: enrollment pending, events this week and next
Every month: certifications expiring in 60 days, attendance patterns by class
Every spring: kindergarten round-up and next year's class sections

The office manager runs cover, the attendance call and enrollment paperwork. The principal approves events, reads attendance patterns and owns certifications. Teachers report absences early and keep sub folders ready. The facilities lead owns requests and event set-up.
Children appear here by first name and last initial only. Health details, custody papers and records stay in your student information system, not here. Share this workspace with staff only.
Rename grades, rooms, credentials and event kinds to match your school and delete the sample rows once your own are in. Edit any cell in place; every count and rate updates on its own.
The school at a glance. Charts read the live tables.

text.text: The first hour decides the school day. By 9:30 every classroom has an adult, every absent child's family has been reached, and the principal knows anything unusual.
for today gets a substitute now: call the sub list in order, then ask a specialist or the instructional coach.
for room changes, visitors and buses.
marked Urgent: a leaking sink or a broken lock is handled before children arrive.
Front door staffed; visitors sign in and wear a badge
Late arrivals sign in at the office and get a tardy slip
Medications handed to the nurse, never left in backpacks
Teachers take the morning count by 8:45. The office enters each class's numbers in
For every absence without a parent call, phone home by 10:00. A child who is missing and unexplained is a safety matter, not paperwork.
Excused absences are those reported by a parent with a reason your district accepts.
Missing ten percent of school days, about two days a month, is chronic absence and hurts reading.
on each class and the Dashboard chart show where to look. The principal and teacher call the family together; ask what is getting in the way and offer help, not blame.
Enrollment calls and walk-ins are logged in
Early pickups only to adults on the pickup list, with ID.
Notes for the principal: anything unusual

At 7:20 the Grade 4 teacher texts that she is sick. The office manager logs it as needing cover, calls the first sub on the list who accepts by 7:35, and marks it covered with the sub's name. At 8:50 the Grade 3 count shows one unexcused absence; a call home finds the child has a fever and the absence becomes excused.
Every event at school affects teaching time, families and the building. Plan it once in
, tell everyone in good time, and nobody is surprised.
with its kind, date and time, place and expected count.
The principal approves it against the testing calendar and other events.

Permission slips home three weeks ahead, back one week ahead
Buses booked; chaperones screened under district rules (one adult for every 10 students, fewer for kindergarten)
Medications, allergy plans and a first aid kit packed by the nurse
A list of every student and every phone number with the lead teacher
Students who cannot go have a supervised plan at school
Pick a time working parents can make, usually 6:00 pm. Offer interpreters for the languages your families speak (see
in Enrollment). Food helps attendance more than anything else.

State testing and reading assessments are events too. Block the window, keep assemblies and trips out of it, and plan quiet halls.
Set-up checked an hour ahead by the facilities lead

The Grade 3 science museum trip is planned six weeks out. Slips go home in English and Spanish, five chaperones complete screening, two students with allergy plans travel with the nurse's kit, and the bus is booked. The trip leaves at 8:30 with all 52 students and returns before dismissal.
An uncovered classroom costs children a day of learning and stretches every other teacher. A simple, practiced cover routine keeps the school calm when people are out.
When a teacher will be out
Teachers report planned absences (training, family, jury duty) in
as soon as they know, with the reason.
Sudden illness: a text or call to the office by 6:45 am.
The teacher leaves sub plans in the shared folder and ticks
The district substitute system, or your own sub list, starting with subs who know the school.
A specialist teacher or coach whose schedule allows.
Combining classes, only for a short time and never above the room's safe limit. Mark the class
The principal or assistant principal teaches.
Every classroom keeps one, up to date:
Class list with photos and any allergies or medical plans
Daily schedule, specials and lunch times
Emergency procedures and the room's exit route
Two or three students who can help and a buddy teacher next door
Simple lessons that work for any day
A sub who has a good day comes back. Greet them, give them a badge and the sub folder, introduce the buddy teacher, and ask how it went at the end of the day.
count on each class and the Dashboard show which weeks need more subs booked ahead: training days, flu season, the week before winter break.

On Monday three teachers are out: one sick, one at training, one on jury duty. Two are covered by subs from the list before 7:30; the third class is taken by the reading coach, whose small groups move to the afternoon. Every absence shows covered by 7:45.
